consensus_summary: Multivalent symbol with two leading strands—Word/gospel of God sown in hearts (explicitly defined in the sower parable) or offspring/descendants culminating in the messianic Seed (Gen 3:15; Gal 3:16)—plus common secondary senses of death/resurrection, faith/kingdom growth, children of the kingdom, and sowing-reaping; no exclusive single meaning.
book_summary: A generative word or life planted to reproduce after its kind, instantiated as God’s word (sower), children (wheat/tares), the promised Messiah, and a planted person growing into a house/people/nation-tree.
consensus_core_identification: Context-dependent symbol whose primary referents are the Word of God or messianic offspring/Christ
book_core_identification: Generative word or life planted to reproduce after its kind
boundary_disagreement: Book unifies the consensus’s separate strands under one creation principle (‘after its kind’) and explicitly elevates personal-to-corporate growth (person → house/people/nation-tree) as a core case rather than a secondary illustration.
rationale: Both identify the same principal biblical cases (word, children of the kingdom, Messiah). The book does not replace those referents; it supplies a single generative category drawn from Gen 1 that the consensus never articulates as the common core, thereby broadening the category while retaining and slightly extending the covered instances. Differences are therefore boundary/precision refinements, not contradictions or novelty.
strongest_objection: Consensus treats the meanings as discrete, context-bound alternatives rather than interchangeable instances of one ‘reproduce-after-its-kind’ principle, so the unification may over-systematize.
